title: Election Eve: Webb County Votes Tomorrow — Mayor, Council, Senate and TX-28 on One Ballot
excerpt: Webb County voters go to the polls tomorrow, Tuesday, November 3, for a joint general election that will decide Laredo's mayor, four City Council seats, a munic
content:
Webb County voters go to the polls tomorrow, Tuesday, November 3, for a joint general election that will decide Laredo's mayor, four City Council seats, a municipal judge — and, on the same ballot, a U.S. Senate seat and the TX-28 House race.

Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., and voters in line by 7 p.m. can still cast a ballot. Texas requires an approved form of photo identification to vote in person, and voters should confirm their assigned polling place before heading out through the Texas Secretary of State's My Voter Portal at VoteTexas.gov.

Early voting closed Friday, October 30, with 46,332 ballots cast — 45,483 in person and 849 by mail — according to KGNS, citing the Webb County Elections Administration. The final day alone produced 6,130 votes, the highest single-day turnout of the two-week period.

The mayor's race is citywide, with five candidates on the ballot: incumbent Mayor Victor D. Treviño, City Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa, JD Gonzalez, Jorge A. Garza and Alfonso “Poncho” Casso. Voters will also decide City Council Districts 1, 2, 3 and 6, and Municipal Court Judge, Place 1.

Beyond City Hall, Webb County voters will weigh in on the U.S. Senate race between Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, and the TX-28 House contest. Mail-in ballots must reach the county early voting clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day, or by 5 p.m. Wednesday, November 4, if postmarked by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

The stakes are local and immediate: the next mayor and council will face Laredo's water, streets and growth questions, while the federal races will shape how the border region is represented in Washington. One open thread remains after tomorrow — District 8 voters get their own special election December 5, with early voting November 23 through December 1.
